findings: The same HTML host-element mismatch was captured with the Footer fiber attached to the correct footer, but its Container fiber claimed the nested grid and the grid fiber claimed the logo wrapper. The next expected div then encountered the logo anchor.

The actual Footer still contained its original Container, grid and logo wrappers in normal nesting; captured nodes were connected. No intercepted JavaScript append/remove/replace call touched the Footer, and the retained mutation records contained additions with no removals.
The timing experiment increased reproducibility. At the actual throw, document.readyState was already complete, so these captures do not establish that the parser was active at that exact moment.

React issue 37321 describes a plausible upstream hydration/parser interleaving failure, but an upstream cause is not proven by these captures. System theme was the fixture; correlation does not prove a theme defect.

nextExperiment.change: One explicit React Suspense fallback=null boundary around the existing async Footer in Chrome; preserve all provider placement and Footer markup.
nextExperiment.validationRequired: Unchanged native loading under the full browser suite, followed by the same cached-script timing probe and no-JavaScript Footer visibility.
nextExperiment.status: The Footer-only boundary was rejected. The broader document-readiness gate plus synchronous Footer presentation passed final source e8e511e validation recorded below.

footerBoundaryExperiment.conclusion: The mismatch moved to the home hero section while document parsing was incomplete. A Footer-only Suspense boundary did not fix the broader timing-sensitive hydration failure, and its pending fallback also broke no-JavaScript visibility.

changes: DocumentHydrationGate around the existing body provider tree uses public React.use with one cached DOMContentLoaded Promise before any child host claims while the document is loading. SSR and already-parsed navigation return the same children with no new Suspense wrapper.

Footer content is loaded before presentation; the synchronous client Footer receives plain serialized labels/legal/year/payment-presence values and retains its existing DOM. The rejected Footer Suspense fallback was removed.

gateChecks: SSR emits identical content without a wrapper or hidden fallback.
The original server button survives suspended initial hydration and its actual handler attaches after DOMContentLoaded, with no recoverable hydration error.
Already-parsed documents attach client interaction immediately.

validatedMitigation.interpretation: These checks validate the mitigation for the reproduced local timing condition and tested user journeys. They do not prove that an upstream React issue is the sole cause, nor guarantee every future browser/network condition. No React/Next scheduler or package source was patched.
validatedMitigation.historicalStatus: Historical source-e8 result only. A later source32c4b65 Node24 eight-worker run captured one further actual React418 on initial Finnish PDP; the body-only gate was subsequently refined. Earlier passing observations remain valid for that original environment but do not establish final-source reliability.

node24Recurrence.interpretation: One initial PDP418 was masked in the test summary by a later unfinished-stream caption timeout. Other trace steps also show large browser-library/test-runner completion gaps; that separate transport/worker stall does not dismiss the captured418. Cause of those delays was not established.

finalWholeDocumentGate.change: The same transparent public React.use document-readiness gate now wraps the entire html element, so html/body host claims also wait until parsing completes. No additional Suspense wrapper, timer, hydration-warning suppression, scheduler patch or SSR markup was introduced. The synchronous Footer remains.
finalWholeDocumentGate.wholeDocumentUnit: tests/unit/document-hydration-root.test.ts hydrates the actual document container, retaining original html/body/button identities, observing no handler while loading and a real handler after DOMContentLoaded, with no recoverable errors.

ambientConditions.scope: Team build/test/browser work was coordinated. Unrelated host workloads were not stopped, and full-host CPU isolation is not claimed.

finalWholeDocumentGate.interpretation: The complete final local CI-equivalent browser suite and targeted slow-PDP regressions pass for this source/runtime. They validate tested behavior, without proving the exact upstream React cursor mechanism or guaranteeing every concurrency/network condition. The earlier eight-worker failure and failed Footer-only Suspense experiment are preserved.
